extracted.intended_audience: readers of Nature: scientists, researchers, and informed public
extracted.subtask_description: Short-form news, notices, and reviews summarising recent scientific papers, meetings, datasets, instruments, and books across multiple disciplines; intended to inform researchers and educated readers about progress and standards. Contains brief critiques and expectations for reporting and publication practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potassium estimation — chloroplatinate precipitation conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Fresenius recommended that in presence of sodium the chloroplatinate should be precipitated in 70 per cent to 80 per cent alcohol; subsequent workers advised the use of absolute alcohol, but this causes analytical problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to Fresenius's original procedure (70–80% alcohol). If absolute alcohol is used, a much larger proportion of platinum chloride is required to ensure complete transformation of sodium chloride into its chloroplatinate salt, and results are generally high owing to co-precipitation of some sodium chloride. Therefore use 70–80% alcohol to obtain accurate results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuity, frequency and station coverage for meteorological observations
rubrics_metrics.description: Meteorological summaries are marred when only a few stations can provide a continuous record for even a short period; value depends on continuity and adequate temporal sampling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure observations come from sufficiently many stations with continuous records over a useful period; use appropriate observation frequency (e.g., three times a day or hourly, as relevant) and a geographically well-scattered network to make summaries valuable and comparable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation and engagement with prior literature in biological/observational papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should reference and be aware of relevant previous work (example: omission of Imms's paper in a paper on ox-warble fly larvae is a notable oversight).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey and cite existing literature on the same subject, compare methods and conclusions with prior studies, and explicitly address discrepancies or corroborations; failure to do so suggests unfamiliarity with the field and weakens the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theoretical paper presentation: state assumptions and limits; consider accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The paper on thermoelectricity 'does not claim to be free from assumptions which are not altogether justified' and the deduced property 'may be open to question.' The reviewer asks whether the theory could be 'thrown into a less analytical form.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theorists should clearly state and justify assumptions, discuss their possible limitations or consequences, and where helpful present ideas in less highly analytical (more accessible or conceptual) forms so readers can assess validity and implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comet reporting: provide orbital elements, daily ephemeris, charts, and perihelion date
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'new set of elements and a daily ephemeris for comet ... are published' and 'a part of the ephemeris is given here; and, in order to facilitate the location of the object, the daily positions ... are marked on the accompanying chart.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting a comet, publish a full set of orbital elements, a daily ephemeris, charts showing daily positions relative to surrounding stars, and indicate predicted perihelion (or perihelion passage) date to facilitate locating and following the object.

rubrics_metrics.name: Astronomical transit reporting: include central transit times and geometric details
rubrics_metrics.description: Transit tables for Saturn's satellite Titan list central transit times, distance from centre (N/S), semi-diameter and semi-duration values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide precise central transit (or occultation) times, distance from centre (with direction), semi-diameter and semi-duration (or equivalent geometric/timing measures) to permit accurate planning and comparison of observations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for an international interdisciplinary journal
rubrics_metrics.description: The Rivista di Scimta is described as an international journal taking a broader view of science, with a table of contents spanning mechanics, energetics, organic chemistry, biology, economics, history, pedagogy, etc., and 'nearly every nationality is represented among the contributors.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A journal aiming to be international and interdisciplinary should include broad subject coverage, represent multiple nationalities among contributors, provide diverse article types (reviews, notes, critical essays), and make clear its international editorial and content scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical thoroughness and expert authorship in mineral-resource reports
rubrics_metrics.description: The US Geological Survey 'mineral resources' volumes present each chapter as a census of production for the calendar year, edited overall and with chapters written by statistical experts; new commodities and consumption figures are included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compile up‑to‑date, detailed production and consumption figures; structure chapters as statistical censuses authored by specialists; include newly relevant commodities or topics (even preliminary) to provide comprehensive coverage of the industry's status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instrument and apparatus catalogues: full particulars, clear arrangement, illustrations
rubrics_metrics.description: Marconi's catalogue 'provides full particulars as to a variety of induction coils... The list is conveniently arranged and admirably illustrated.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Catalogues of scientific instruments should supply full technical particulars for each item, be conveniently organised for the intended audience, and be well illustrated to aid users (e.g., medical men or experimentalists) in selecting appropriate apparatus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidebook/handbook utility: practical information for intended audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Handbooks (e.g., 'Handbook of the Federated Malay States' and 'Bradshaw's Through Routes') are commended for practical information — for settlers, tourists, teachers — including cost estimates, maps, plans, and useful vocabularies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Travel or regional handbooks should include practical information tailored to their audience (settlers, tourists, teachers): cost estimates for enterprises (e.g., starting a plantation), clear maps and plans, useful vocabularies, and concise guidance on local suitability of crops or activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weather reporting: include comparisons with long-term records and anomaly quantification
rubrics_metrics.description: The weather summary references maximum/minimum temperatures, comparisons with observations since 1841, 'defect of temperature on the mean for the period', aggregate rainfall vs. normal, and notes on sunshine deficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weather summaries should present key statistics (max/min/mean temperatures, rainfall totals, sunshine) and compare them to long-term averages or records, quantify deviations (e.g., degrees below mean, inches less than normal), and discuss likely outlooks based on those comparisons.
